'''''Tradescantia spathacea''''', also called the '''oyster plant''',<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=505554#null | title=ITIS - Report: Tradescantia spathacea }}</ref> '''boatlily'''<ref>{{PLANTS |id=TRSP8 |taxon=Tradescantia spathacea |accessdate=14 December 2015}}</ref> or '''<nowiki/>'Moses-in-the-cradle'''', is an herb  in the [[Commelinaceae]] family which was first described in 1788. It is native to [[Central America]].<ref name=net/>

The plant's common name "[[Moses]] in the Cradle" is due to its small, white flowers within a boat-shaped, purple bract that resembles a cradle, which is a visual resemblance to the biblical story of [[Moses]] in the bulrushes, where he was placed in a basket.<ref>[https://wildroots.in/shop/indoor-plants-for-home-and-offices/foliage-plants/moses-in-the-cradle-tradescantia-spathacea-or-rhoeo/#:~:text=The%20name%20%E2%80%9CMoses%20in%20the,diarrhea%2C%20decongestant%2C%20and%20expectorant. Moses In The Cradle (Tradescantia spathacea or Rhoeo)] by Wild Roots. Retrieved July 14, 2025.</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Starr 080607-7174 Tradescantia spathacea.jpg|left|thumb|The compound inflorescence inside [[bract]]s which lend the name "boat lily" and "Moses-in-the-cradle"]]
''Tradescantia spathacea'' has fleshy [[rhizome]]s and [[Rosette (botany)|rosettes]] of waxy lance-shaped leaves. Leaves are dark to metallic green above, with glossy purple underneath. These will reach up to {{cvt|1|foot|order=flip}} long by {{cvt|3|inch|order=flip}} wide. They are foliage plants that reach a height of around {{cvt|1|foot|order=flip}}. The short-stemmed [[perennial]] shrub grows in a dense clump and forms a [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of thick, lanceolate or linear leaves, about 30 cm long and 7 cm wide, facing upward, which are dark green above and purple below. The color of the underside is due to certain pigments, [[anthocyanins]]. Some varieties, such as 'vittata', have longitudinal yellow stripes on the upper side of the leaf.<ref name=net>[https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Tradescantia~spathacea Tradescantia spathacea Sw.] Plant Net.  Retrieved July 14, 2025.</ref>

The flowers are very small, white and clustered, arise in axillary [[cymes]] enclosed in purple, boat-shaped [[bracts]] (giving their common name, Moses-in-the-Cradle). The flowers appear from spring to autumn.<ref>[https://primexgardencenter.com/plant-care-sheets/moses-in-the-cradle/#:~:text=Tradescantia%20Spathacea%20commonly%20known%20as,the%2DCradle%20their%20common%20name. Moses in The Cradle] Primex Garden Center. Retrieved July 14, 2025.</ref>

==Distribution==
It is native to [[Belize]], [[Guatemala]], and southern [[Mexico|México]] ([[Chiapas]], [[Tabasco]], and the [[Yucatán Peninsula]]) and is widely cultivated as an ornamental houseplant; it has become naturalized in parts of coastal [[Southern California]], [[Florida]], [[Hawaii]], [[Louisiana]], [[Texas]], and various Pacific and Indian Ocean islands.<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=270451 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Tradescantia%20spathacea.png Biota of North America Program 2013 county distribution map]</ref><ref>Hunt, D. R. 1994. 257. Commelinaceae. 6: 157–173. In G. Davidse, M. Sousa Sánchez & A.O. Chater (eds.) Flora Mesoamericana. Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, México, D. F.</ref> 

==Cultivation==
[[File:Tradescantia spathacea Philippine Pde Palm Beach Gold Coast IMGP2943.jpg|thumb|Cultivar with pink and light green leaves]]
They are hardy in [[Hardiness zone|USDA zones 9-12]] and are also grown as ornamental houseplants. Its cultivar 'Sitara' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AGM Plants July 2021 © RHS – ORNAMENTAL |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=21 December 2021 }}</ref> In Mexico, it is used in traditional medicine as a [[medicinal plant]] for sores and wounds, as well as an [[antiseptic]] and [[anti-inflammatory]].

== Invasiveness ==
''Tradescantia spathacea'' has naturalized in parts of coastal [[Southern California]], [[Florida]], [[Hawaii]], [[Louisiana]], [[Texas]], and various [[Pacific Islands|Pacific]] and [[List of islands in the Indian Ocean|Indian Ocean islands]] and is listed as a Category II invasive exotic species by the Florida Exotic Pest Plant Council. "This means Invasive exotics that have increased in abundance or frequency but have not yet altered Florida plant communities to the extent shown by Category I species. These species may become ranked Category I if ecological damage is demonstrated."<ref>{{cite web |author1=Florida Exotic Pest Plant Council |title=Florida Exotic Pest Plant Council's 2017 List of Invasive Plant Species |url=http://bugwoodcloud.org/CDN/fleppc/plantlists/2017/2017FLEPPCLIST-TRIFOLD-FINALAPPROVEDBYKEN-SUBMITTEDTOALTA.pdf |accessdate=14 March 2019 |language=en |date=2017}}</ref>
